text_blocks.snippet: High blood pressure (hypertension) is often called the "silent killer" because it typically causes no signs or symptoms at all, even when readings reach dangerously high levels.
snippet_highlighted_words: no signs or symptoms at all

text_blocks.snippet: In rare cases where blood pressure spikes significantly or becomes severe, some people may experience subtle or overt warning signs:

list.snippet: Headaches (especially severe or occurring in the early morning)
Pounding sensation in the ears, neck, or chest

text_blocks.snippet: A blood pressure reading higher than 180/120 mm Hg combined with acute warning signs is a medical emergency. According to the American Heart Association, you should call 911 immediately if you have a reading over 180/120 and experience:

list.snippet: Chest pain or severe back pain

text_blocks.snippet: Because symptoms are rare, regular monitoring is vital. You can learn more about risk factors and management at the Mayo Clinic or read guidance from the National Council on Aging.
If you or someone else is experiencing an emergency, please call emergency services right away. Otherwise, tell me:

list.snippet: What your recent blood pressure readings are (if you have them)
What specific symptoms you are currently feeling

text_blocks.snippet: I can help you understand when it's time to call a doctor.
